requirements.requirement: Create the appworker account on node1
requirements.summary: useradd -m -s /bin/bash appworker executed successfully; id and getent passwd confirm uid=1000(appworker) exists both before and after the node restart.

requirements.requirement: Limit appworker login sessions to 8192 open files (nofile)
requirements.summary: /etc/security/limits.d/90-appworker.conf sets soft and hard nofile to 8192; a real login shell (sudo -u appworker -i) shows ulimit -Sn and -Hn both returning 8192, confirmed pre- and post-restart.

requirements.requirement: Limit appworker login sessions to 256 processes (nproc)
requirements.summary: Same limits.d file sets soft and hard nproc to 256; login-shell ulimit -Su/-Hu confirm 256, verified pre- and post-restart.

requirements.requirement: Provider-wide node-restart evidence protocol on node1 (independent of task contract)
requirements.summary: Pre-restart healthy baseline captured (boot_id bf4e9cbb..., account/limits verified), systemctl reboot issued and acknowledged, connectivity loss observed during the reboot window, new boot_id 13cd0c31... confirmed post-restart, and account/limits state re-verified as recovered. Fixed lifecycle snapshots independently corroborate the boot-identity change (bf4e9cbb... -> 13cd0c31...) and show no failed services or package-health regressions after executor.

overall_summary: The executor created the appworker account on node1 and applied a limits.d drop-in enforcing both soft and hard nofile=8192 and nproc=256, verified through an actual login shell's ulimit output both before and after a full node restart. The mandatory restart-evidence protocol was completed correctly, with a healthy pre-restart baseline, an acknowledged reboot, a genuine boot-identity change (corroborated independently by the fixed lifecycle snapshots), and recovered account/limits state post-restart. No unnecessary or unreverted mutations were found.
limitations: Verification relied on ulimit output from a login shell rather than inspecting a live process's /proc/<pid>/limits, though this is a standard and sufficient method for confirming PAM limits.d application.
The task instruction did not itself require a restart; restart evidence was collected solely to satisfy the independent provider-wide protocol and does not affect the material task outcome scoring.

operational_hygiene.summary: All state-changing commands were directly tied to task outcomes or the mandatory restart protocol: user creation, limits.d file write, and the systemctl reboot with its acknowledgement/polling. The four 'failed' commands (cmd-ddd1848fe42e4775, cmd-572b9f876c464f08, cmd-d3ac90a721aa4a5e, cmd-1c6eba9f25864572) were read-only boot_id polls that failed only because the node was mid-reboot (connection reset/timeout) — expected discovery during a bounded disruption, not unnecessary mutations or task failures. The lifecycle diff between after_prepare and after_executor shows only the expected boot-identity change, port-holder PID churn from restarted sshd/chronyd, and systemd-private tmp directories tied to the new boot — all inherent to a legitimate reboot, with no failed services, no package-health regression, and no abandoned or unrelated files.
